source.title: FSI Swahili Basic Course
source.attribution: Foreign Service Institute (U.S.), Swahili Basic Course, 1963.
source.normalization: Dialogue lines were read from the Internet Archive OCR of the printed course and normalized for OCR spacing and obvious character errors. Only the short public-domain dialogues are reproduced; summaries and quiz questions are original Bolingo Learn writing.

lessons.title: FSI 1 · Morning greetings
lessons.summary: Two men greet each other in the morning. Jambo works at any hour; Habari za asubuhi? asks specifically for the morning's news, and Njema answers that all is well.

lessons.title: FSI 2 · Daytime greetings
lessons.summary: The daytime greeting swaps Jambo for Hujambo? — literally “do you have no trouble?” — and answers Sijambo, “I have no trouble.” Habari za mchana? asks after the day's news.

lessons.title: FSI 3 · Evening greetings
lessons.summary: Evening greetings follow the same pattern with Habari za jioni? (How is the evening?) or Habari za usiku? (How is the night?). Habari njema answers “the news is good”.

lessons.title: FSI 4 · Greeting a lady
lessons.summary: A man greets an older woman as mama (ma'am, mother), and she answers Sijambo. The morning question and answer stay the same, so only the address changes.

lessons.title: FSI 8 · Breakfast at the hotel
lessons.summary: At a hotel breakfast, the waiter asks Je, unataka chakula? (Would you like food?). Kuna chakula gani? asks what is available, and Tafadhali, niletee mayai orders eggs politely.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.sw: Kuna matunda na uji na mayai.
dialogue.en: There is fruit, porridge, and eggs.
